title: The Father and His Sons (Bundle of Sticks)
summary: An aging father had three sons who were constantly quarreling with one another. No day passed without bitter arguments, insults, and petty jealousy tearing the peace of their house...
keywords: the father and his sons (bundle of sticks)
full_text:
An aging father had three sons who were constantly quarreling with one another. No day passed without bitter arguments, insults, and petty jealousy tearing the peace of their household apart. The father's gentle counsel and stern warnings were ignored, and he grieved deeply knowing that after his death, their discord would bring about their financial and social ruin.

Feeling his end draw near, the wise father called his three sons to his bedside and ordered a servant to bring in a tightly bound bundle of hazel sticks.

Handing the bundle to his eldest son, the father said: "My son, take this bundle and break it in two."

The eldest son strained with all his might, bracing his knee against the sticks, but the bundle remained intact. The second and third sons tried in turn, sweating and straining every sinew, but neither could break the tightly bound sticks.

"Now," said the father, "untie the cord and hand one stick to each brother."

The sons did so. "Now break your stick," commanded the father. With a simple snap of their wrists, each son shattered his single hazel twig with effortless ease.

The father smiled tenderly and said: "Behold, my sons! You are like these sticks. If you remain bound together in brotherly love, mutual loyalty, and unity, no enemy on earth will ever be strong enough to break you. But if you divide your strength through petty strife, you will be broken as easily as those solitary twigs!"
moral: United we stand, divided we fall; strength lies in unbreakable harmony.
